clue.text: Strong beneficial quality — or lack of it?

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical abbreviation for strong or loud
utility is the quality of being useful or beneficial

explanation.surface: Someone muses on a powerful virtue and wonders whether it is really missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: 'it' is the beneficial quality just named, and its lack is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Futility is uselessness, the absence of the usefulness the clue has just described.

clue.text: Participating in slalom, I go downhill — what a surprise!

indicators.note: the letters take part in the run of words slalom, I go downhill, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A skier on a slalom course heads downhill and exclaims in astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a text-speak spelling of 'oh my God', an expression of shock or surprise.

clue.text: Tree, old one

definitions.meaning: the sweet or horse variety of nut-bearing tree
a stale, much-repeated joke or story

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a nut tree and a hackneyed old joke told too often.

clue.text: Brute bites bottom of intruder, bit of a chicken?

indicators.note: the brute closes its jaws round the next letter, so it holds it inside

parts.note: a brute is a beast

indicators.note: the last letter of intruder, its bottom in a down clue

explanation.surface: A savage animal sinks its teeth into the backside of a trespasser, perhaps one stealing poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: Ins R (the bottom letter of intruder) into BEAST. The question mark marks the definition as one example of a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The white meat from the front of a fowl is one of the standard cuts of a chicken.

clue.text: Poor clubs supplied with card game

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit
rummy is a card game of melding sets and runs

explanation.surface: A weak hand in clubs is dealt during a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Crummy is informal for shoddy or of low quality, a synonym of poor.

clue.text: Composer's composition central to feature

indicators.note: the composition sits in the middle of the facial feature

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
op., opus, is a numbered musical composition

explanation.surface: A remark that a composer's work is the heart of some programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Frédéric Chopin was the Polish Romantic composer of piano works.

clue.text: Man in Roman emperor dissolving an imperialist government

indicators.note: the man is placed inside what is left of the emperor
the word an melts away from the emperor's name

parts.note: Trajan was Roman emperor from AD 98 to 117
he is a man, the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man inside a Roman emperor's realm as an imperial administration is broken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dissolving an' reads as the empire breaking up, but it tells you to take the two letters out of the emperor's name; 'in' then houses the man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Raj was British imperial rule over the Indian subcontinent until 1947.

clue.text: Spooner's supportin' Scotland as potential shocker

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, as this phrase asks us to do

parts.note: backin' is a clipped form of backing, supporting
the Jocks is informal for the Scots, the Scottish team or people

explanation.surface: Someone cheering on Scotland as a possible shock result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backin' the Jocks', with the B and J sounds swapped, says 'jackin' the bocks'.
explanation.definitionFit: The spring-loaded toy that leaps out of its box is designed to startle, a shocker in waiting.

clue.text: Twice married, be desired, when drunk — legless, perhaps?

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger into a new arrangement
the abbreviation for married is used two times

explanation.surface: A man wed twice is longed for and, after drinking, is legless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legless' looks like slang for drunk, which fits the surface, but here it means limbs cut off. MM with BE and DESIRED is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with limbs cut off has been dismembered, and losing legs is one example of this.

clue.text: Woodworm's work routine

definitions.meaning: woodworm make tunnels by drilling into timber

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the act of drilling holes and an adjective for dull, tedious things.

clue.text: Way to cut back, cutting front, for example

indicators.note: the way slices into the middle of the other word
the first letter is chopped off the synonym for back

parts.note: to back a venture is to finance it
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: Advice on how to trim expenses, starting with the most visible ones, as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like part of 'cut back', but it is the verb: FINANCE less its front F gives INANCE, which ST cuts into.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case or example of something.

clue.text: Bird given fruit

definitions.meaning: the flightless bird of New Zealand
the furry brown fruit with green flesh, also called the Chinese gooseberry

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the flightless New Zealand bird and the furry green-fleshed fruit.

clue.text: Ultimately, Lembit impressed by topless dress worn by cheeky girl following party chief whip?

indicators.note: the girl and her outfit come after the party

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the dress is inside the girl, as clothing is worn

parts.note: a minx is an impudent girl

indicators.note: the letter is pressed into the dress
the dress loses its top letter

parts.note: a sari is an Indian dress

indicators.note: the final letter of the word Lembit

explanation.surface: A tabloid tale of politician Lembit Opik smitten with a scantily dressed Cheeky Girl after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Lembit Opik, a Liberal Democrat MP, dated a member of the pop duo the Cheeky Girls. T goes into ARI to make ATRI, which goes inside MINX.
explanation.definitionFit: A dominatrix wields the whip in sadomasochistic play, hence a whimsical chief whip.

clue.text: Bring order to a mess (it's yet to be ordered)

indicators.note: the letters are still waiting to be put in proper order

parts.note: the contraction gives its letters with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone sees a jumble that has not yet been sorted and resolves to tidy it.
explanation.walkthrough: A, MESS, ITS and YET are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To systematise is to arrange according to a system, putting things in order.

clue.text: Lament refurbishing trendy home? Not me!

indicators.note: refitting and redoing suggests the letters are rearranged
the letters of me are excluded from the word home

parts.note: home is taken as written before me is removed

explanation.surface: A grumble about doing up a fashionable house, from someone who wants no part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: HOME without ME leaves HO, which joins TRENDY in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnody is a song or poem of mourning, a lament for the dead.

clue.text: See 24
Italian port, where Irish erected something in "The Italian Job"

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are raised, reading upwards

parts.note: the 1969 film The Italian Job features a famous car chase in Minis

explanation.surface: A question about an Italian location where an Irishman built a prop for a classic heist film.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a resort and port on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Relax, filling in edges of trickier puzzle

indicators.note: the synonym for relax fills the space between the edges
the first and last letters of trickier

parts.note: to ease off is to relax

explanation.surface: Advice to calm down while completing the border of a tougher puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: EASE fills T...R, the edges of trickier.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser is a tricky puzzle or brain-teaser.

clue.text: Religious official on coke, perhaps, sticks nose in on top of table

parts.note: someone on cocaine is high
to pry is to be nosy

indicators.note: the first letter of table

explanation.surface: A churchman snorting cocaine, nose to the table top.
explanation.definitionFit: The high priest was the chief priest of the Jewish temple, a senior religious official.

clue.text: Pillbox like a pillar box, creating ill-feeling

parts.note: a pillbox is a small round hat
British pillar boxes, the roadside postboxes, are painted red

explanation.surface: A small round box resembling a postbox causes resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pillbox' suggests a pill container or concrete gun post; here it is the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatred is intense dislike, a strong form of ill-feeling.

clue.text: See 7
Old artist making comeback, not finished

indicators.note: the artist's name is read backwards
the last letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Edgar Degas was the French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: An elderly painter returns to work with a canvas left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: DEGAS less its final S is DEGA, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means elderly, a synonym of old.

clue.text: Interval is time interrupting social occasion

indicators.note: the pieces break into the middle of the social occasion

parts.note: a dance is a social gathering

explanation.surface: A break in the evening where the clock cuts into a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interval' and 'time' look like one idea; the definition means a space between points, while 'time' is just its abbreviation, put with 'is' inside the occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A distance is a space or interval between two points.

clue.text: Boy, where are 'er eggs laid?

parts.note: the dropped-h 'er stands for her, given as ER
a nest is where eggs are laid, framed by where are

explanation.surface: A colloquial question about where a hen has put her eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where are ... eggs laid?' points at NEST, with 'er placed before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this is a traditional male first name, so it stands for any boy, as in Oscar Wilde's play title.

clue.text: Actress with whom I mix while on location in Somerset

parts.note: to meld is to blend or mix
as can mean while, at the same time as
Taunton is the county town of Somerset, in south-west England

explanation.surface: An actress with whom the speaker mingles during a shoot in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On location' sounds like filming jargon, which fits the actress, but 'on' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Imelda Staunton is an English actress, known for Vera Drake and The Crown.

clue.text: Decoration attached in time

indicators.note: the word for attached goes inside the time

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time
on means attached, as in a lid that is on

explanation.surface: A medal pinned on in due course.
explanation.definitionFit: An honour is an award or decoration such as a knighthood or medal.
